title: One shared hardened unsigned-commit helper; config refusal names the real file and null reads as unset
action: Review B-P2-1 + B-P2-4. Part A (mechanism): add one shared helper in worktree/git.rs — commit_unsigned(cwd, message, pathspec: Option<&str>) -> GitOut — spawning git commit with --no-gpg-sign and stdin null; close.rs's bookkeeping commit and phases.rs's merge commit both call it. Do NOT change any user-facing failure text (R81 pins close's exit-status spelling — close keeps formatting its own reason from GitOut fields; fail_text stays for merge). The two gpg stub-proof tests must stay red-capable: verify once by removing the flag inside the helper (both red), restore, note in trace. Part B (config): close_commit_bookkeeping_invalid_value hardcodes .bee/config.json in its message while reading the merged overlay (state.rs merges config.local.json over config.json) — make the refusal name the file actually carrying the offending value (check local first, then main); Value::Null now reads as UNSET (defaults on) instead of refusing — null is bee's unset idiom; every other non-boolean still refuses up front. Restore a direct test on the defense-in-depth fallback arm of commit_close_bookkeeping (non-boolean reaching it returns config_off) lost in the cbh-1 retarget. TDD: local-overlay repro (bad value only in config.local.json -> refusal names config.local.json); null test (close proceeds); existing refusal + stub tests green.

truths: both commit paths go through one shared hardened helper and both stub-proof tests stay red-capable
a bad value living only in config.local.json is refused naming config.local.json
null close_commit_bookkeeping behaves as unset (on), not a refusal

artifacts.substantive: commit_unsigned helper consumed by both callers, plus tests

trace.outcome: shared commit_unsigned helper in worktree/git.rs consumed by close + merge (single-flag removal reds both stub tests); config refusal names the offending file across the overlay; null reads as unset; defense-arm test restored
